meta.title: Shree Siddhivinayak
meta.institution: Shree Siddhivinayak Ganapati Temple Trust, Prabhadevi
meta.location: S. K. Bole Marg, Prabhadevi, Mumbai
meta.foundedNote: The trust identifies first consecration as 19 November 1801; a Maharashtra district statistical publication gives the same date. The original 1801 document was not inspected.
meta.intro: Siddhivinayak at Prabhadevi is a permanent Ganesh temple whose surviving institutional history connects an early nineteenth-century shrine to a major rebuilding in the 1990s. Its right-trunk black-stone icon remained central as the surrounding structure changed. This collection follows the temple, its architecture and public-service institutions, with dated exterior photographs rather than an invented sequence of annual festival idols.

sections.title: From a small shrine to a public institution

paragraphs.text: The trust dates the first consecration to 19 November 1801 and says the date appears in government records. A Marathi Mumbai City district statistical publication also identifies that day and names Laxman Patil and Deubai Patil. These are retrospective accounts; the underlying early document has not been examined here. The collection therefore records the established institutional date without claiming to possess the foundation deed.

The trust’s published Act provides a different kind of evidence: it records a 16 June 1936 High Court consent decree placing administration with the Official Trustee. The statute, titled the Shree Siddhi Vinayak Ganpati Temple Trust (Prabhadevi) Act, 1980, received presidential assent in January 1981 and reconstituted management for wider welfare activity. This legal chronology concerns governance, not the first installation of the deity.

sections.title: The icon stayed as the building changed

paragraphs.text: The trust describes a single black-stone image, about two and a half feet high, with the trunk turning right. Its four hands hold a lotus, axe, rosary and modak; Riddhi and Siddhi flank it. These are the iconographic identifiers of an enduring temple image. Neither the temple’s annual festivals nor the dated photographs below imply that a new central idol is made and immersed each year.

The architecture account credits Sharad Athale and records renovation beginning in 1990, with construction described as taking three years. It separately dates the crown installation and Kumbhabhishek to 13 June 1994. The new multistorey, multiangular structure used marble and pink granite while keeping the idol intact. The trust cites Ambernath’s Shiva temple as a climatic design reference and credits Suresh and Mitesh Mistry for the sanctum frame.

The district administration's published history identifies 27 April 1990 as the foundation-stone ceremony for the expanded building and 13 June 1994 for the crown ceremony. These dates describe the rebuilding around an existing shrine. The new exterior sequence records several later viewpoints and a decorated interior, rather than a succession of newly made annual idols.

The trust’s activity statement combines Maghi and Bhadrapad Ganeshotsav with cultural programmes, medical assistance, dialysis, health camps, a book bank and libraries. Its architecture account locates reading and study facilities within the expanded complex. These are institutional descriptions of its public-service role; the present collection has not audited current beneficiary numbers, expenditure or operational hours.

claims.text: 19 November 1801 is the consecration date maintained by institutional and government retrospectives.
The trust’s statutory history recites a 1936 administration decree and an Act titled 1980 with assent in 1981.
The 1990s building programme retained the existing icon.
Medical and educational programmes are described by the trust itself.
The 2006, 2008 and 2012 photographs show the post-rebuilding permanent structure; the 2018 image shows its temporary decoration.
